subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should an ignore file exceeding 4 MiB cause the scanner to exclude that directory subtree terminally, rather than retain prior effective scanning behavior or use a different recovery contract?
rationale: The cap prevents unbounded memory use, but the chosen fail-closed behavior can make an existing workspace subtree disappear from discovery and therefore needs explicit owner acceptance.

options.title: Approve terminal 4 MiB denial
options.body: Keep the bounded reader and terminal subtree exclusion, then require refreshed exact-head workspace-scan proof before merge.

options.title: Choose another oversized-file contract
options.body: Specify a different observable fallback and update the implementation, tests, and proof to match that compatibility decision.

recommendation.title: Approve terminal 4 MiB denial
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded reader and terminal subtree exclusion, then require refreshed exact-head workspace-scan proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch’s final behavior-defining commits and assignment both point to steipete as the best available decision owner.
